note: Run these in a local Claude session with blender-mcp connected and the user's test .blend open. The geometry itself is covered headless by scripts/selftest.py.

evals.prompt: I've put the cursor on the cart path on hole 4 where the ditch runs under it. Add a 600mm concrete pipe culvert and blend it into the meshes.
evals.expected_output: Asks for the library location at session start; runs scene_report; plans a pipe (span 0.6) and asks the user to confirm the AUTO axis; builds and shows both mouths; backs up, blends, verifies (ok=true); finalises into the nearest Concrete mesh only after approval.

evals.prompt: stick a 4ft stone arch under the bank at the cursor, the burn runs roughly north east to south west. headwalls need to sit flush with the bank
evals.expected_output: Uses kind='arch', span=T.ft(4), bearing about 225 (flow NE to SW) or asks which way the water flows; mentions the arch will read as concrete once joined; checks flush_max_error in verify.

evals.prompt: Add a 24 inch corrugated steel pipe at the cursor. I've dropped CULVERT_IN and CULVERT_OUT empties at each end of the run-off so use those.
evals.expected_output: plan_culvert(kind='corrugated', span=T.inch(24), inlet='CULVERT_IN', outlet='CULVERT_OUT'); reports the fall between the empties and warns if it is less than 1 in 100.

evals.prompt: C01's outlet headwall looks too tall, knock a foot off it and redo the blend
evals.expected_output: Uses restore('C01') (the terrain is already blended), edit_plan('C01', out_top_rel=<current - 0.3048>), then build, backup, blend and verify again; does not hand-edit meshes.
